purpose: Phase-8A treatment-exposure abstraction: ORDINAL exposure status / stage / relative intensity describing how much EFFECTIVE (intracellular) treatment the surviving population has experienced. Effective exposure is derived from validated upstream delivery/uptake/intracellular engines - NOT from applied topical amount. A high applied dose with low intracellular availability yields LOW effective exposure. Schematic normalized values only; no dose (mg), concentration, AUC, or real duration (all NOT_REPORTED).

coefficient_policy.valid_range: relative_exposure_intensity in [0,1]; cumulative_exposure is a bounded normalized accumulator in [0,1]
coefficient_policy.1_interpretation: 1 = maximal schematic effective exposure the model represents
coefficient_policy.source: normalized modeling abstraction over validated upstream effective-availability outputs
coefficient_policy.sensitivity_note: intensity scales pressure only through effective exposure; it does not itself classify resistance.
coefficient_policy.limitations: No dose / concentration / AUC / real time; ordinal only.

single_exposure.meaning: One treatment episode in progress or completed.

repeated_exposure.meaning: Multiple discrete treatment episodes have occurred.

washout.meaning: Treatment withdrawn; recovery interval in progress.

rechallenge.meaning: Renewed treatment after a washout interval.

exposure_stage.note: Ordinal progression driven by validated simulation-stage advancement, never wall-clock time.

rules.effective_not_applied: exposure intensity reflects EFFECTIVE intracellular availability (upstream), not applied topical amount.
rules.cumulative_bounded: cumulative_exposure is a bounded normalized accumulator, never an unbounded sum.
rules.deterministic_history: exposure progression is deterministic and serializable; no RNG, no wall-clock time.
